correctness.rationale: The flip-equivariant map identification is checked directly against the magma product. Any two-sided factorization weakens c, a and d+a; conversely selecting distinct intermediate image orbits gives a genuine equivariant U∘Tf∘V factorization with fixed-source constraints and free-orbit orientations accounted for. The feasibility condition d−c+a≤N is necessary and constructive; summing the eligible triples gives the polynomial. Regularity d=c follows from the exact existence of an equivariant image section. A standalone verifier exhaustively compares ideal inclusion for all 16 elements at n=2 and verifies thousands of constructive factorizations at n=3,4,5; finite tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 pairmorph paper completely describes one-sided Green preorders, but the investigated primary passages state neither the exact three-invariant two-sided preorder nor the polynomial count of all principal two-sided ideals. The new orbit-resource factorization is required to establish the iff, and the admissible-triple count is not one of its left/right-class enumerations. The 2026 idempotent study and the 2023 finite G-set study address separate invariants. Bounded source and indexed-record searches found no earlier statement; the 2022 precursor was accessible only through secondary abstracts, a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: The complete 2022 precursor and 2023 dissertation were not directly inspected; a stronger comparison could alter the originality assessment.
A more general theorem on J-preorders of finite G-set endomorphism monoids may imply the explicit special-case formula but was not located in the bounded search.
The published 2026 journal article was accessible only as abstract; its accessible arXiv primary text was inspected substantially, with some later paragraphs not directly read.

value.rationale: The 2026 literature motivates exact Green and ideal structure of a natural and rapidly growing monoid. Previously available left/right ideal characterizations do not directly give the two-sided ideal poset. The new law gives a complete J-order by only three computable ranks, distinguishes regular/nonregular types, and turns a potentially enormous monoid of n^(n²) operations into a closed polynomial class count; it is useful for further ideal lattice and representation-theoretic calculations. It does not claim the easy consequence D=J or finite computational novelty as sufficient by itself.
